title: The Best GRC Software in 2026
summary: Compare GRC software by what you actually need: a first SOC 2, multi-framework mapping, or enterprise risk. Includes pentest, audit cost, and who the tool is for.
body_markdown:
For most organizations, the best governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software depends more on use case than on speed, price, or brand. But not every GRC tool is the same.


Several solutions with overlapping capabilities now share the GRC platform category, including enterprise GRC suites, compliance automation platforms, and security-first compliance software. Yet with so many options, some teams feel more uncertain than ever about which GRC platform to choose.


This guide is written for SaaS teams that need a first SOC 2 report, multi-framework control mapping, or enterprise risk without standing up a GRC department. It explains what GRC software is and compares the best GRC tools, including Oneleet, Scrut, Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto, Delve, ServiceNow GRC, Archer, MetricStream, OneTrust, Optro, SimpleRisk, and Eramba. Most importantly, it evaluates each platform against criteria that reflect what most SaaS companies actually need.


## **The Best GRC Software: Key Takeaways**


The best GRC software depends on the use case – who the tool is for and how they intend to use it. To help companies choose the right GRC tool, we’ve sorted the top contenders into platform categories. They include:


-


**Security-first compliance software:** Best for companies that need the report and packet to survive a buyer’s security review. Examples include Oneleet and Scrut.


-


**Compliance automation platforms:** Best for companies that need to produce a report with audit evidence collected via integration. Examples include Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto, and Delve.


-


**Enterprise GRC suites:** Best for companies with multiple business units and a dedicated GRC team. Examples include ServiceNow GRC, Archer, MetricStream, OneTrust, and Optro.


-


**Free and self-hosted:** Best for small teams with limited budget and someone on staff to run it. Examples include SimpleRisk Core and Eramba Community.


For most SaaS teams, the platform that produces evidence a security team will actually accept is more valuable than the one that collects evidence fastest.


## **What Is GRC Software, and What Do Most GRC Tools Actually Do?**


GRC software replaces the spreadsheets and inboxes where a company's policies, risks, controls, evidence, and audits would otherwise live. Originated by the[Open Compliance and Ethics Group in 2002](https://www.oceg.org/ideas/what-is-grc/) , GRC is defined as the capabilities that enable an organization to "reliably achieve objectives, address uncertainty, and act with integrity."


GRC software is where a company keeps its policies, risks, controls, evidence, and audits, instead of using spreadsheets and inboxes.


Because the definition is broad, many organizations conflate tools with fundamentally different capabilities into a single category. But in reality, many solutions sold as ‘GRC software’ can’t solve a SaaS team’s biggest challenges. That includes:


-


**First-time SOC 2:** Many startups and SaaS teams need a first-time SOC 2 report to close an enterprise deal. But[most GRC software only produce the report](https://www.oneleet.com/blog/real-security-vs.-badge-security-what-enterprise-buyers-actually-do-with-your-soc-2-report) , not the evidence a buyer’s security review is likely to request, like a penetration test.


-


**Multi-framework mapping:** Many SaaS companies must comply with[multiple frameworks](https://www.oneleet.com/frameworks) that have overlapping requirements, including HIPAA, ISO 27001, and SOC 2. Some GRC platforms deliver those frameworks with the requirements pre-mapped to existing controls, but they often charge an add-on fee.


-


**Enterprise risk:** Some companies need to manage risk across multiple business units, each with its own policies, controls, and audits. At large organizations, that calls for an enterprise GRC suite, a dedicated team to run it, and weeks of implementation. For SaaS teams without a GRC department, these tools can introduce unnecessary complexity.


Only a handful of GRC platforms actually produce the evidence a security team will accept. Instead, most sell what we call security theater – the badge instead of the security the badge is supposed to represent. For example, a SOC 2 report earned with a vulnerability scan in lieu of a penetration test, or a shared inbox in place of a security lead.


## **How to Choose a GRC Platform**


For many organizations, choosing a GRC platform can feel like a chore. With so many options, some teams get overwhelmed trying to find a tool that meets their needs without adding cost or complexity.


To simplify the evaluation process, ask vendors the following five questions.


1.


### **Is the pentest part of the engagement or a separate purchase?**


Not all GRC platforms treat pentesting equally. Some sell pentesting separately through partner firms, while others include it in the engagement. Three things vary from vendor to vendor:


-


**Who performs the test:** The vendor's own testers, a partner firm the vendor refers you to, or an autonomous tool, which is a different product from a manual test.


-


**What the test covers:** Infrastructure-level and application-level testing are separate scopes.


-


**Retesting:** Whether a retest after you fix the findings is included, and for how long.


Once a pentest is complete, the security team reviewing your report will also ask who ran it and what it found. Make sure to[check the tester's credentials](https://docs.oneleet.com/penetration-testing/faq/) , including the industry-standard OSCP and other Offensive Security certifications, such as OSCE or OSWE.


But the report matters as much as the test. A security reviewer reads the findings, their severity ratings, and each remediation status, and asks how recent the test is.


Still, a missing pentest is the[#1 reason we see SOC 2 reports fail](https://www.oneleet.com/blog/do-you-need-a-penetration-test-for-soc-2-compliance) a security review.


→ Ask who performs the test and what certifications they hold, whether it's manual or autonomous, if retesting is included, and how long the retest window runs.


1.


### **Is the audit in the quote or billed by a partner later?**


Some GRC platforms include a SOC 2 audit in the quote, and others offer access to a network of partner auditors. Either way, a[licensed CPA firm](https://www.oneleet.com/blog/soc-2-auditor-certifications-does-it-matter-who-does-your-soc-2-report) performs the audit and issues the report. The difference here is who manages the auditor's requests and whether the quote includes an audit fee.


-


**At platforms that include the audit** , the vendor coordinates the auditor's requests and assembles the evidence packet, and an independent firm performs the audit and issues the report.


-


**At platforms that sell auditor access** , you pick a firm from the vendor's network or bring your own, and that firm bills you separately.


ISO 27001 adds internal, external, and surveillance audits to obtain and maintain the certificate, so a platform's audit support should cover all three.


→ Ask whether the audit is included in the quote and who the auditor is.


1.


### **Who reviews the evidence before the auditor does?**


Software, a person, or both can review evidence before an auditor does. Many GRC tools use integrations to collect the policies, processes, configurations, lists, logs, and samples that prove whether a control is in place. But some evidence, like signed documents, may still need to be uploaded by hand.


-


**An automated check** confirms the basics, such as a resource identifier and a timestamp, and flags gaps.


-


**A human review** addresses auditor questions, such as whether the item shows the control operated during the audit period and who can explain it.


For SOC 2 Type 2, the auditor takes a sample. For each list or log, you provide the full population, and the auditor usually[checks about 10%](https://docs.oneleet.com/guides/what-makes-good-evidence/) . Some platforms describe the review as an AI agent's validation, and others assign a named person before the auditor is engaged.


We think a named person who can answer the auditor's questions reviews evidence better than an AI check alone.


→ Ask whether a named person reviews your evidence before the auditor does.


1.


### **Can one control test satisfy the next framework?**


Some GRC platforms can map one control to multiple frameworks, often as an add-on fee. Others simply require organizations to do that work themselves. Here’s the difference:


-


**A pre-mapped framework** arrives with each requirement already linked to a control and its evidence from day one.


-


**A requirement-only framework** arrives as a list of requirements that teams must manually link to each control before evidence counts.


Pricing typically follows the same split – entry plans cover one framework, and each additional framework is priced as an add-on.


→ Ask whether your next framework is pre-mapped, requirement-only, or a separately priced add-on, and whether a control tested once satisfies every framework that requires it.


1.


### **What does year one cost with everything added up?**


Year-one cost is the platform plus implementation time, the audit, and the pentest. But some pricing pages list auditor access rather than an audit fee.


-


**The platform fee** is the hardest of the four to pin down, simply because most platforms price by quote and few publish an entry price.


-


**Quotes** are usually metered on something that grows with the company, such as employee count, admin users, or the number of frameworks.


-


**Add-ons** such as additional frameworks, vendor-risk monitoring, professional services, or an advanced pentest sit on top.


-


**Implementation** is your own team's time, typically tens of hours for a first SOC 2 program.


-


**The audit** is a separate firm's fee. Some platforms build a vetted auditor's fee into the price, while others sell access to an auditor network and the firm bills you directly.


The pentest is the line most often missing from the quote. At several platforms, a third party runs it as a separate purchase, sometimes at a partner discount, and retests may be limited to a window after the first test. One platform's help center also recommends an annual third-party test, so the line can recur each year.


→ Ask every vendor for one figure that covers the platform, implementation time, the audit, and the pentest, and what that figure is metered on at renewal.


## **The Top GRC Software for SaaS Teams, Reviewed**


The best GRC software for SaaS teams usually falls into the security-first bucket. Unlike compliance automation software, security-first compliance tools bundle the compliance platform, a penetration test, and audit support into one engagement.


### **Oneleet**


Oneleet is a security-first compliance platform for SaaS teams that need a SOC 2 report that passes a buyer's security review, without building a GRC department. One scoped quote covers the platform, the pentest, the[vCISO](https://www.oneleet.com/blog/meet-your-oneleet-vciso) , and audit support, with no surprises.


With Oneleet, you can define a control once and[map it across frameworks](https://www.oneleet.com/compliance-platform) , including SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, CIS IG1, NIST 800-171, and EU DORA, plus custom frameworks.


You’ll also get a named vCISO, who stays for the term starting day one, from signing through renewal. Before engaging an auditor, they’ll coordinate a human review of your evidence, controls, and policies. After that, they’ll join deeper enterprise security reviews, so a buyer asking who owns security can actually meet them.


Every SOC 2 package includes an audit performed by an independent AICPA auditor and the report,[which we coordinate for you](https://www.oneleet.com/framework/soc-2) . For ISO 27001, we help with internal, external, and surveillance audits.


With AI evidence review enabled for your workspace,[Oneleet AI checks each evidence item for the basics an auditor looks for](https://docs.oneleet.com/compliance/evidence/) , and flags problems before you submit. For SOC 2 Type 2, your vCISO also[draws a random sample of up to 25 items from each list or log](https://docs.oneleet.com/guides/what-makes-good-evidence/) to test the population, and a person verifies it before the auditor is engaged.


Every Oneleet plan also includes a[manual, human-led penetration test](https://www.oneleet.com/compare) by testers certified at minimum to OSCP and OSCE or OSWE for the Compliance and Comprehensive packages, and at minimum to OSCE or OSWE for custom pentests. The test itself is a[gray-box test](https://docs.oneleet.com/penetration-testing/pentesting-classification/access-level/) , where the tester has limited access to internal documentation or user credentials, and[retests are free for 12 months](https://docs.oneleet.com/penetration-testing/findings-decisions/) .


After the test, we attach the published report to your "Penetration testing performed" control for your auditor. So when a buyer asks what your last pentest found, you can hand over[a report with risk ratings, findings, and each finding's remediation status](https://docs.oneleet.com/penetration-testing/final-report/) .


→ That’s where Oneleet wins with SaaS teams facing security reviews. The test a buyer will inevitably ask for is already done by[our own certified testers](https://docs.oneleet.com/penetration-testing/ptaas/) inside the engagement.


### **Scrut**


Scrut is an AI[compliance automation platform](https://www.scrut.io/post/drata-alternatives-competitors) that includes all platform modules, auditors, and pen-testers. Its[Security Analyst](https://www.scrut.io/) agent runs agent-driven pentesting, with humans verifying every finding. Scrut also sells[in-house VAPT services](https://www.scrut.io/solutions/iso-27001) from a team accredited by CREST, a not-for-profit cybersecurity industry body.


However, Scrut's pages disagree on what that team covers. Its[CREST announcement](https://www.scrut.io/post/scrut-is-now-crest-accredited) covers vulnerability assessment services. But its[August 5, 2026 cost page](https://www.scrut.io/hub/soc-2/cost-of-soc-2-audit) says Scrut is "CREST-accredited for penetration testing." It also says that "application-level pen testing still requires a third-party vendor".


Scrut's[internal security page](https://www.scrut.io/company/security) says its "in-house VAPT experts hold certifications like CEH, CCNA, and EJPT.” No OSCP, OSCE, or OSWE appears anywhere on its site, and its[frequently asked questions page](https://www.scrut.io/faqs/general) says audit charges may influence the final quote.


→ A security reviewer will still ask whether Scrut's agent-driven platform test or its in-house team ran your pentest, which certifications the testers hold, and who tested the application layer.


### **Vanta**


Vanta is a compliance automation platform that collects audit evidence through integrations. Its[Essentials plan](https://www.vanta.com/pricing) , sold as “the fastest, simplest path to compliance,” covers one compliance framework. Its pricing page lists an AI agent for evidence checks, policy control mapping, and evidence collection, with vendor-risk monitoring as an add-on. Every tier is a personalized quote.


Vanta's[Seamless Audit package](https://www.vanta.com/collection/soc-2/who-can-perform-soc-2-audit) builds a Vanta-vetted auditor's cost into the platform price. No pentest appears on the pricing page, though Vanta's[comparison page against Drata](https://www.vanta.com/compare/drata) marks "Pen test included".


An[August 5, 2025 post](https://www.vanta.com/resources/security-capabilities-for-startups) announced autonomous pentests powered by XBOW, with one free test a year for companies with up to 750 employees on certain plans. However, coverage limits still apply. Other pentests come from[Vanta's partner firms](https://www.vanta.com/resources/how-to-do-penetration-testing) .


→ A security reviewer will still ask who ran your pentest and whether it was autonomous or manual.


### **Drata**


Drata is a[compliance automation platform](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/5329593-frameworks) that automatically collects evidence. Its[automations run deep](https://www.oneleet.com/oneleet-vs-drata) , with frameworks either pre-mapped to its controls or requirement-only. Its[Foundation plan](https://drata.com/plans) covers up to 50 full-time equivalent employees and includes “1 Pre-Mapped Framework”.


Drata works with a curated network of audit firms in its[Auditor Alliance](https://drata.com/products/compliance/audit-hub) , or your own auditor. Pricing is a personalized quote on every tier, and additional frameworks are an add-on.


The plans page never mentions a pentest, but Drata's partner directory lists pentest firms offering Drata-referral discounts. Meanwhile, one[Drata customer describes](https://drata.com/customers/wins/compliance-gated-market-one-founder-no-margin-for-error) “a single offer covering SOC 2, ISO 27001, audit, and penetration testing at a fixed number”.


→ A security reviewer will still ask whether a third party or an internal tester ran the pentest behind the report.


### **Secureframe**


Secureframe suits teams that want a published entry price. Its[Fundamentals package](https://secureframe.com/pricing) starts at $7,500/year. Both it and the Complete packages each list one compliance framework and include access to the Secureframe Audit Partner Network.


Secureframe offers guidance from more than[30 in-house compliance experts](https://secureframe.com/) and former auditors. Its[help center](https://support.secureframe.com/en/articles/15111430-pen-testing-requirements) recommends an annual third-party penetration test and introduces partner firms. More specifically, a[2022 Secureframe post](https://secureframe.com/blog/trusted-partner-program) names pentest partners including Cobalt, Software Secured, and TrustFoundry.


→ A security reviewer will still ask which partner firm ran your pentest and what it covered.


### **Sprinto**


Sprinto is a compliance automation platform. Its[Foundation plan](https://sprinto.com/pricing/) is for startups on their first certification and lists continuous monitoring across 300+ integrations and 25+ frameworks automated out of the box. Its plans include network auditor access or your own auditor.


Sprinto’s pricing page prints no price, though a[blog post](https://sprinto.com/blog/soc-for-cybersecurity/) lists a bundle that starts at $4,900/year. Sprinto's[terms for a one-time VAPT](https://sprinto.com/vapt-terms/) say a third-party provider runs it, with retests available for 60 days. Additional frameworks and professional services are add-ons.


→ A security reviewer will still ask what your one-time VAPT covered and whether you retested within 60 days.


### **Delve**


Delve calls itself “[a compliance partner, not a platform](https://delve.co/) .” Its AI agents validate evidence, and pricing is a customized proposal after a demo.


Delve's[comparison page](https://delve.co/competitors) says every audited framework comes with a complimentary, manual gray-box pentest by GWAPT- or OSCP-certified penetration testers. The same page calls vCISO support in Slack complimentary, while Delve's home page lists an "Advanced penetration test" and "vCISO support" among add-on services.


The[comparison page](https://delve.co/blog/response-to-misleading-claims) also lists audit cost as "Included in price," and independent licensed firms issue the report, from Delve's network or an auditor you choose. A[January 9, 2026 post](https://delve.co/blog/inside-delve-trusted-compliance-process) says that a comprehensive human review occurs before any audit triggers.


→ A security reviewer will still ask who performed your complimentary pentest and which certification they hold.


### **ServiceNow GRC**


ServiceNow GRC fits companies already running ServiceNow. It’s sold as[risk product entitlements on the ServiceNow AI Platform](https://www.servicenow.com/community/grc-blog/getting-started-with-your-servicenow-risk-product-implementation/ba-p/3463683) , with partners in the implementation. Its risk modules include Risk Management, Policy and Compliance Management, Audit Management, Vendor Risk Management, and Business Continuity Management.


### **Archer**


Archer is built for enterprise GRC teams. Its[pricing page](https://www.archerirm.com/pricing) says it's trusted by 37 of the top 50 global banks. Most enterprise deployments go live in[8–12 weeks](https://www.archerirm.com/public-sector-solutions) , by its own estimate, and it runs[on-premises or as SaaS](https://www.archerirm.com/explore-archer) . Pricing is by demo request, with no figure published.


### **MetricStream**


MetricStream is built for large enterprises. Its press kit cites[20+ years of GRC experience and 500+ implementations across Fortune 1000 companies](https://assets.metricstream.com/pdf/insights/metricStream-press-kit.pdf) . Pricing starts with[a request form](https://info.metricstream.com/ms-pricing.html) , and no figure is published.


### **OneTrust**


OneTrust sells[Tech Risk & Compliance](https://www.onetrust.com/solutions/tech-risk-and-compliance/) as one package among several, with 55+ ready-to-action frameworks. Its[pricing page](https://www.onetrust.com/pricing/) bases the package's price on admin users and asset inventory, with no figure listed.


### **Optro (formerly AuditBoard)**


Optro, formerly AuditBoard, describes itself in a[March 9, 2026 post](https://optro.ai/blog/what-is-optro) as an AI-powered GRC platform that provides "GRC intelligence through a GRC system of action". Its home page says it's[trusted by over 50% of the Fortune 500](https://optro.ai/) . But its[pricing page](https://optro.ai/pricing) shows a form and no figure.


### **SimpleRisk**


[SimpleRisk Core](https://www.simplerisk.com/pricing) is free, open source, and self-hosted, with unlimited users. Paid packages start at $5,000 a year, and it publishes every price on its pricing page.


### **Eramba**


Eramba's[Community edition](https://www.eramba.org/eramba-software) is free on-premises. Enterprise costs €2,500 a year on-premises or €5,000 a year as SaaS with EU or US hosting. Its[FAQ says](https://www.eramba.org/faqs) both editions are accessible with open code, but are not open source. Eramba also says it is not a vulnerability management tool, and its site shows no pentest.

## **The Best GRC Tools by Company Stage**

A first certification needs a report that passes a buyer's security review, a second framework needs controls mapped once across frameworks, a security-led team needs a manual pentest, and a company already on an enterprise suite starts with that suite.

### **Under 50 People, First Certification**


If the buyer will read your pentest report, pick Oneleet. If only the report matters and a partner firm can supply the pentest,[Vanta Essentials](https://www.vanta.com/pricing) ,[Drata Foundation](https://drata.com/plans) , or[Secureframe Fundamentals](https://secureframe.com/pricing) fit.


By our own published estimate, implementing SOC 2 controls takes 20–100+ hours, usually about 40–60, and most companies get through that implementation in 4–6 weeks. A Type 2 observation window then follows, typically 3 months for a first report and 12 months for renewals.


### **50–250 People, Second Framework**


For a second framework, pick a platform that maps one control across frameworks. That way, the controls you've already tested count toward it. We map a control once across SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.


### **Security-Led Teams**


Look for a manual test by a credentialed tester, with retests included and the report attached to the control your auditor will read.


### **Already Running ServiceNow**

## **GRC Software Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Is Vanta GRC software or compliance automation?**


Vanta is a compliance automation platform with GRC modules on top. Its[Essentials plan](https://www.vanta.com/pricing) covers one compliance framework.


### **Do small companies need GRC software?**


Small companies need GRC software once an enterprise deal depends on a SOC 2 report and the security evidence behind it. What they don't need is an enterprise GRC suite built for a dedicated GRC team. Our answer is a security-first compliance platform with a manual pentest and a vCISO.


### **How much does GRC software cost in year one?**


Year-one cost includes the platform, implementation time, the audit, and the penetration test. Ours is a single quote for the platform, the pentest, the vCISO, and audit support.


### **Are there free or self-hosted GRC tools?**


Yes. SimpleRisk Core and Eramba's Community edition are free to run on your own servers. But neither includes an auditor or a penetration test. So, the audit, the pentest, and the person running the program are still on you.
